thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike of CUDA OOMs on runtime-pool-usw2-*: 12 OOMs/min across 4 nodes. Monitoring shows per-node "reported headroom" >= 1.1GB but processes still fail with CUDA OOM. tagging oncall.

sre-oncall: I'm looking. node ids: gpu-node-77, gpu-node-85, gpu-node-92, gpu-node-93. Seeing container restarts for runtime-service. Any recent deploys? :eyes:

deploy-bot: recent rollout completed 12:05 UTC to runtime-service v2.14. no rollbacks.

maria (eng-runtime): Not aware of a change that should affect alloc. Will pull logs. Can someone paste the OOM stack traces?

lex (eng-sre): grabbing logs from gpu-node-85 now. Quick heads-up: nvml reports free memory ~1.2GB but allocator logs show fragmented free blocks and many small reserved blocks pinned.

kevin (eng-ml): This matches a pattern we've seen where KV cache reserves nibble memory leaving unusable fragments under certain prefetch patterns.

joel (customer-ops): Heads-up: two customers (acct-9843 and acct-2201) reported 503s to their inference endpoints ~12:07-12:16 UTC. Potentially impacted more.

sre-oncall: timeline so far: alert 12:06 -> first OOM 12:04 on gpu-node-77 -> traffic surge at 12:03 to big-batch workloads. I'm going to drain gpu-node-85 from scheduler.

sre-oncall: `rdctl drain-node gpu-node-85 --nowait` -> cordon+evict in progress.

maria (eng-runtime): pulling allocator debug from node-85:
```
[allocator] requested 2048MB -> allocate() failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[allocator] headroom_report: free=1280MB, largest_free_block=512MB, reserved_blocks_total=896MB (count=14)
[kvcache] prefetch_window=1024 tokens -> pinned_reserve=768MB
```

maria (eng-runtime): Notice reserved_blocks_total + largest_free_block + active usage > nvml free, fragments leave no contiguous block for large allocations.

lex (eng-sre): So NVML shows 1.2GB but largest contiguous chunk is 512MB -> allocation for a single tensor (size ~1.6GB) fails.

kevin (eng-ml): Possible contributors: continuous batching creating large transient kv cache requests + prefetch spikes. We saw this in 2025 but we had a mitigation to cap prefetch/reserve. Did that change? 

maria (eng-runtime): It looks like runtime config `KV_PREFETCH_ENABLE=true` and `RESERVED_BLOCK_TARGET_MB=1024` on these nodes. I'd like to temporarily lower reserved blocks and force KV cache eviction.

sre-oncall: Action plan:
- reduce reserved target on affected nodes
- evict kv cache on node(s)
- drain additional nodes if needed
- if still failing, fallback entire pool to smaller-max-batch model

lex (eng-sre): I'll patch node labels to avoid new large-batch routing for the pool. `route switch runtime-pool-usw2 -> runtime-pool-usw2-smallbatch` (partial).

maria (eng-runtime): Executing commands:
```
rdctl set-node-flag gpu-node-85 RESERVED_BLOCK_TARGET_MB=256
rdctl kvcache-evict --node gpu-node-85 --all
```

sre-oncall: Done for node-85. Watching.

(5m)

sre-oncall: OOMs dropped to 1/min on node-85. Node-77 still noisy. I'll do same on 77 and 92.

maria (eng-runtime): Running eviction + reserve tweak on 77 and 92 now. Also enabling a conservative allocator fallback: `ALLOCATOR_CONTIGUITY_CHECK=1` to prefer allocating from coalesced spans.

kevin (eng-ml): Also recommend disabling prefetch temporarily: `KV_PREFETCH_ENABLE=false` for the pool — that reduces pinned_reserve quickly.

sre-oncall: Applied prefetch=false on pool. Traffic shifted; error rate decreasing.

joel (customer-ops): Customer-impact update: acct-9843 reports degraded latency but no data loss; acct-2201 still sees intermittent 503s but improving. I'm sending an update to both now.

joel (customer-ops): "We're investigating transient GPU memory errors causing retries — engineers are actively mitigating. We'll follow up when stable." :white_check_mark:

maria (eng-runtime): After evict+config changes, telemetry shows contiguous largest_free_block increased to ~1.8GB on node-85 and allocations succeed. Adding a short-term guard to runtime to refuse >1.6GB single-tensor requests when fragmentation suspected.

lex (eng-sre): Next steps: schedule an eng-runtime deep dive post-mortem. We need longer-term fixes: smarter reservation accounting (track contiguous free spans), proactive coalescing on free, and better prefetch throttling.

maria (eng-runtime): Logging ticket: RWD-ENG-7762 - Investigate allocator fragmentation under KV prefetch. Assigning to runtime team.

sre-oncall: Final status 12:40 UTC: OOM rate back to baseline, pool serving but with temporary prefetch=false and reserved target reduced. Nodes 77/85/92 drained+repopulated one-by-one. No lost PII. Customers alerted and on a follow-up.

kevin (eng-ml): Adding note: add eval harness that simulates batch+prefetch to reproduce fragmentation in CI.

sre-oncall: Handing off to night oncall @lex. All clear for now but postmortem and patch are required.

lex (eng-sre): taking over. I'll coordinate the postmortem and keep customer-ops looped in. Thanks team. :pray:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: severity downgraded to P2 at 12:45 UTC. Root cause suspected: high prefetch + reserved-block sizing -> fragmentation caused large contiguous allocation failures. Follow-up: RWD-ENG-7762, schedule allocator patch and prefetch throttle."
